params._comment: Physical parameters for tools/gen_rhodes.py. ALL VALUES ARE PRIORS (ESTIMATE) until the reference fit (IMPLEMENTATION-v3 §7) replaces them.
params._doc_levels: gain_target_dbfs: RMS (50..300 ms) of one voice at v = 100, every key exactly; set so a 4-note chord at v = 127 peaks near -3 dBFS (host, effects bypassed). peak_dbfs: a global cap on 90 % of the keys single-voice v = 127 peaks (+3 dB); it does not bind at this target.

bands._doc: hammer tip bands: first MIDI key of each band (A0 = position 1 of R05 W1)
bands._doc_tip: hammer tips per band (Rhodes service manual ch. 4, R05 W1/W2): Shore A durometer of the neoprene (null = maple wrapped in shrink tube) and tip size (inch). The Hertz contact stiffness follows from them (gen_rhodes.band_K).

hammer._doc: Hammer = a rigid mass at the tip on a Hertz rubber tip, F = K e^1.5 (1 + alpha de/dt) (Hunt-Crossley), against the tine's first 6 FE modes. Effective mass = min(mass_kg, m_tine1 / m_eff_ratio) (gen_rhodes.hammer_mass): 11 g (R02 Tab. 3.2) in the bass, where the contact then lasts ~5.7 ms at v = 100 (Muenster & Pfeifle 2014 measured 6.42 ms on average), down to ~0.5 g in the treble, where a heavier hammer followed the tine and re-struck it 2..12 times (the FM-1 scan's 23 dB holes). alpha: neoprene loss (s/m, ESTIMATE). E_wrap: the wood band's wrapped-maple face (Pa, ESTIMATE). v_max, range_db: hammer speed at v = 127 and its range (dB) down to v = 1.

jitter._doc: S2, per-key deterministic jitter (gen_rhodes.jit: a hash of seed, key, quantity; uniform in +-1 x the amount): t60_pct V1's T60 (and the overtones'), level_db the key's gain, off_gap the pickup offset (gap units), contact_pct the hammer contact rate (via the tip stiffness K, contact time ~ K^-0.4), beat_pct and w_pct the whirl's beat rate and weight. Never V1's pitch.

pickup._doc: pole radius / gap per family; family 0 = 1/16 inch gap, family 1 = 1/32 inch gap. Family 1: R = 1 gap (R03 code geometry: a 1 mm pole radius at a ~1 mm gap). Family 0 has the same pole piece at twice the gap (gap_rel 2), so in its own gap units R is half (0.5) and every vertical offset (off_gap, TYPE, TONE, the cap) is halved (geometry, no recording; S8). R = 2 gave a non-monotonic velocity response (2026-10-15 test).

release_t60._doc: damper-on T60 (s) by MIDI upper bound. 2026-11-08: shorter, a felt that stops the tine within tens of ms (before: 0.5 / 0.4 / 0.3 / 0.2, jRhodes sfz)

strike._doc: strike point from the clamp (m) at key 21 and key 108, linear in key (R05 W1)

strike_fit._doc: S2 (0.9.10): O1 (the tine's 2nd mode, 6.3-6.9 f0, inharmonic) per key no stronger at v = 127 than tine_v127_points (dB: its band 6.3-7.7 f0 in 0-20 ms re the 30-300 ms H1; gen_rhodes.strike_fit; only ever turned down from the physics). Measured targets: E4-A5 about -39, C6-E7 about -65; the tables had -17 / -28 (the inharmonic ring of a hard upper-register strike).

t60_v1._doc: sustain T60 of V1 (s) at MIDI keys, log-interpolated; flat below the first point, halving every halve_keys above the last (floor). 0.9.10 (2026-11-08): the mid / upper register longer, keys 32-43 slightly shorter; before: Shear 2011 tine Q (1974 Mark I), T60 = 6.908 Q/(pi f0) (research/09)

tinebar._doc: bar_cents_points: [midi, cents of the bar's own f0 relative to the tine] (Muenster & Pfeifle ISMA 2014 Table 1, research/09); k_rel coupling rel. to w_t^2 (ESTIMATE); mu bar/tine mass (ESTIMATE); tine T60 = target; bar T60 multiple (ESTIMATE)

tip_peak_gap_v127._doc: V1 tip peak (gap units) at v = 127: bass .. treble

tone._doc: The TONE knob (params.c P_TONE) moves the pickup offset: below the middle (v <= 64) by (v - 64) / 128 gap (down to -0.8 gap total on STAGE 77: round, mellow); above it by up_gap over the upper half, so the top stops short of the pole axis (offset 0), where the pickup's response is even and the fundamental cancels (0.9.4 went to +0.19 gap: the fundamental fell 28 dB at v = 104 and the level 14 dB, then came back past the axis). off_max_gap caps every voice's offset (key + TYPE + TONE; DYNO's +0.1 would reach the axis), checked by tools/types_ab.py.

types._doc: Physical voicing per TYPE, relative to the STAGE 77 priors. off: pickup offset change in gap units (+ = toward the pole axis: H2 up, fundamental down, 'bell'; - = off-axis: round, mellow; W6). bark: tip displacement / gap scale (pickup distance: closer = more bark and output, W3); the gain is compensated by 1/bark. ham: hammer contact-rate scale (felt tips 1970-71 are softer: longer contact, fewer high partials; W2/W9). bell: tine overtone (O1/O2) force scale. rlc: pickup inductance x cable/input capacitance resonance [f_hz, q]. body: up to 2 biquads after the load: [kind, f_hz, q, gain_db], kinds hp2 / peak / lshelf / hshelf; the amp and speaker of the instrument (Suitcase: Peterson preamp into four 12-inch speakers, W5/W6: the closed cabinet's 250 Hz box bump and the cones' roll-off, a high shelf -5 dB at 5.5 kHz (0.9.5; before, a 50 Hz high-pass, which the load and the master DC blocker already do); Dyno-My-Piano: active treble-boost preamp). level_db: output trim so the types play at matched loudness (measured A3 v100 + A4 v70, host).

v2_drop._doc: O1: keys whose V2 slot (the tone-bar mode, 0.4-0.8 f0, its tip weight 60 dB or more under V1) is left out: a mode loop fewer per voice. Chosen by tools/rh_nulltest.py (the C engine, each key alone, v100 and v127, re the tables with the mode): every listed key's residual <= -60 dB of the note. Keys 100-108 keep it (-60.8 .. -47 dB at v127: the short top notes leave the slower bar mode audible in the tail). On keys 29-39 rhodes.c's gate (RH_V2_GATE_LO/HI) already stopped it. Keys 40-84 hold the beat partner instead (whirl).

velocity_trim._doc: small per-key RH_PAMP trim at the velocity anchors so each key's level curve (re v = 104) follows the median curve of all keys (monotonic). The physics (hammer_contact) is already even to ~3 dB; the trim is bounded to +-max_db and reported in rhodes_spec.json (pulse.pamp vs pulse.pamp_phys). iterations 0 = physics only.
velocity_trim._doc_target: the level curve (dB re v = 104 at the V_ANCH velocities) each key's RH_PAMP trim aims at, one row per iteration: frozen at the median curve of the 0.9.5 tables (2026-10-24), so a change to some keys (the top-key fix, the per-key jitter) no longer moves every other key through the median. Remove it to recompute the median of all keys (gen_rhodes prints it).

voicing._doc: pickup voicing: H2/H1 (dB, 30..300 ms) of a v = 100 strike per key; each key's tip scale (b) is set to it (gen_rhodes.voice_pickups). A Rhodes at mf is mostly fundamental (R05 W3: the bass voiced for 'mostly fundamental'; W6 E3: fundamental loudest); the bark grows with the tip swing toward v = 127. Replaces tip_peak_gap_v127 as the b scale (that one only sets the starting point).

whirl._doc: S1, the beat partner in the V2 slot (gen_rhodes.whirl): keys [lo, hi] (V2 absent outside: O1); w = its weight re V1 (the envelope ripple is about 20 log10((1 + w) / (1 - w)) dB peak to peak, the pitch excursion at the ripple's trough w / (1 - w) x beat Hz), tapered to w / (taper_keys + 1) at the ends; beat_hz_points [midi, Hz] (|f(V2) - f(V1)|, the wobble's rate); t60_ratio [lo, hi]: its T60 re V1's, seeded per key in the range. pitch_cents_max: the beat is lowered where w / (1 - w) x beat would swing the pitch more than this (the bass keys; measured swings run ~15 % over it). The two tuning knobs: w and beat_hz_points. keys 40-84: rhodes.c's V2 gate ends at 39 (RH_V2_GATE_HI) so the slot runs there; the partner on 40-48 costs ~+94 us in the 9-bass-note v127 block (tests/c/rh_cost.c), taken on the FM-1's measured margin (2026-10-24: whole ISR 3516-3640 us at 10 voices).
